result.detail: The model is written per bit, straight from the spec text: detection uses the current mode and the remembered level, detection beats a clear, an acknowledge of a number >= N does nothing, and reset beats writes. Each directed test also checks literal values, so a test cannot pass just because the model and the RTL share a mistake. Single faults I expect the suite to catch include: reversed priority (T7), clear winning over set (T3/T4/T6), edge sources treated as level (T4), irq ignoring ENABLE (T3/T5), an acknowledge clearing extra bits or accepting numbers >= N (T5), and wrong upper-bit masking (T2). This is unverified until someone runs mutants. The clock period is 40 ns, so all reads in a cycle fit before the next falling edge. The biggest risk is the nonce plusarg name. If the platform's name differs, only the top module's $value$plusargs chain needs to change. A tech lead can confirm the name.
